title: Safeguard: regional flip automation generator for Private VPC failover drills
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Overview:
Implement a reusable Terraform-driven generator that composes and schedules end-to-end private VPC 'region flips' for multi-region DR rehearsal. The generator produces opinionated IaC artifacts and a small control-plane job that executes an automated sequence: preflight validations, staged traffic flip (canary -> partial -> full), post-flip health validations, and rollback on failure.

Why this work:
- Current DR rehearsals are manual, brittle, and require deep ops involvement.
- Teams deploying Redwood Private lack a repeatable, auditable mechanism for exercising cross-region restores and DNS/GRP switchover behaviors.
- Automating these rehearsals reduces time-to-detect infra regressions and validates upgrades and configuration changes under realistic load.

Scope:
- Terraform module library that generates a region-flip execution plan for a customer VPC topology (subnets, LB targets, DNS entries, routing policies).
- A lightweight 'flip controller' job (stateless function + small state in SSM/ParamStore) that runs the plan and records events to the Console audit log.
- Health gates that include application-level checks (smoke endpoints), KV/redis cache warm-up checks, and token-level request sampling to ensure ML model RPCs are returning expected latency and error rates.
- Integration with existing rollout features: canary percentages, rollout windows, and automatic rollback policies.

Out of scope:
- Implementing customer-specific model migration logic.
- Full UI in Console (we'll expose a minimal connector; Console work is separate).

Deliverables:
- Terraform module(s): vpc_flip_generator, flip_preflight_validators, flip_dns_sweeper.
- Flip controller: small Lambda/Container job + state schema (ParamStore keys).
- Test harness: synthetic traffic runner and smoke-test checklist that can be invoked by the generator.
- PRD + runbook documenting how to schedule, audit, and interpret flip runs.

Acceptance criteria:
- The Terraform generator can output a complete flip plan for a sample private deployment topology with >= 2 regions.
- A scheduled flip run executes the stages (preflight -> canary -> partial -> full -> post-validation) and writes step-level events to the Console audit log.
- The flip controller triggers automatic rollback when any health gate fails and records failure reasons and metrics to the DR dashboard.
- The flip plan supports a dry-run mode that performs preflight checks without touching DNS or routing.
- Modules include clear inputs for DNS TTL, canary percentage, allowed maintenance windows, and pre-approval tokens.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- We will implement the generator as Terraform modules that emit a JSON 'execution plan' using terraform-local-exec; this keeps intent declarative and auditable. Trade-off: introduces a thin imperative step during apply.
- Preflight validators will include both infra-level checks (subnet reachability, route table ACLs, LR endpoints) and application-level checks (smoke endpoints, model RPC latency profiling). Validations should be idempotent and fast (< 60s aggregate) to keep preflight cheap.
- DNS switchover will favor low-TTL records where possible; for customers with constrained DNS control we will support provider-specific API-driven updates (Route53, Cloud DNS).
- For final traffic routing we will use weighted LB or traffic proxy approach instead of IP-level BGP manipulation to reduce blast radius.
- Persistence: minimal ephemeral state stored in ParamStore with a tombstone marker on completed runs for auditability. Consider moving to an internal DR runs table later.

Telemetry and success metrics:
- Per-run: start/end timestamps, per-stage duration, rollback cause (if any).
- SLA checks: post-flip P50/P95 latency vs baseline, 5xx error delta, token consumption.
- Number of rehearsals run per quarter (target > 2 per critical customer).
- Mean time to detect configuration regressions introduced by recent infra changes.

Security and compliance:
- Flip runs must be restricted to specific service principals; Terraform module will accept a DR role ARN.
- All changes are gated behind approval tokens for production-like environments (manual or automated approvals supported).
- Audit events forwarded to customer KMS-wrapped logs where required.

Rollout strategy:
1) Alpha: internal Redwood testbeds (1 customer-like env) — validate generator and controller.
2) Beta: opt-in customers with engineering involvement — iterate on validators and DNS integrations.
3) GA: expose Terraform modules and minimal console connector; document pre-reqs and runbook.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Terraform-local-exec introduces drift if controller changes independently. Mitigation: enforce plan-only dry-run CI job and store generated plans in Git.
- Risk: DNS propagation causing partial traffic mix that breaks model stateful caches. Mitigation: include KV cache warm-up stage and canary traffic sponge to exercise model cold-start paths.
- Risk: accidental double-run. Mitigation: plan locks via ParamStore/LK and tenant-scoped run IDs.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 - scaffolding (2 sprints):
- Design Terraform module interfaces and example inventory format.
- Implement vpc_flip_generator that produces an execution JSON plan.
- Implement basic flip controller prototype (Lambda) and ParamStore state schema.

Phase 2 - validators & DNS (2 sprints):
- Implement preflight infra validators and application smoke checks.
- Add Route53 & CloudDNS update adapters; implement dry-run locking.
- Add metrics emission to DR dashboard.

Phase 3 - traffic choreography & rollback (2 sprints):
- Implement staged weighting logic and canary runner (synthetic traffic runner).
- Add automatic rollback triggers and post-mortem scaffold.

Phase 4 - Beta + docs (1 sprint):
- Run with 2 opt-in customers and iterate.
- Finalize runbooks, PRs, and Console connector hooks.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for Terraform modules (plan output schema).
- Integration tests: run generator against test VPC and simulate flip with synthetic traffic.
- Chaos tests: artificially fail health gates and ensure rollback triggers and audit events recorded.
- Load validation: run canary traffic generator with representative token rates and verify latency distributions.
